text:
sasha: Heads-up — p95 east-west latency spike in gpu-pool-2 during the 11:30–11:45 batching ramp. App traces show tail tokens delayed by ~40–120ms. Anyone seeing infra noise? :thinking_face:
ops-bot: ALERT: east-west-p95 > 45ms on cluster/gpu-pool-2 for 15m. Affected nodes: node-gpu-07,node-gpu-10,node-gpu-12.
liam: I pulled dmesg + ethtool from node-gpu-10, seeing repeated link flaps for mlx5_core around the same time. Also counters show tcp_retransmits spiking.
rita: ran a quick iperf between node-gpu-07 -> node-gpu-10 during a repro window: 1) throughput normal 2) latency p95 jumps with bursts. Screenshot: https://internal/diag/iperf-run-176451 (attached).
henry: tcpdump snippet from node-gpu-10 at 11:36 shows duplicate ACKs followed by RTOs — looks like packet drops not just queuing. Snippet:
```
11:36:12.123456 IP 10.0.4.7.52014 > 10.0.4.10.52014: Flags [.], seq 13024:13152, ack 4421, win 64240, length 128
11:36:12.123789 IP 10.0.4.10.52014 > 10.0.4.7.52014: Flags [.] ack 13024, win 64240
11:36:12.124012 IP 10.0.4.7.52014 > 10.0.4.10.52014: Flags [.] seq 13152:13280, ack 4421, length 128
11:36:12.124345 IP 10.0.4.10.52014 > 10.0.4.7.52014: Flags [.] ack 13024, ack 13024, ack 13024
```
liam: that looks like hardware-level retransmits. Can you paste ethtool -S and 'cat /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/log_level' from the node? Also what MTU are we using?
sasha: MTU is 9000 on those nodes (we rolled jumbo frames for high throughput).
rita: quick check: jk, one of the k8s kubelet nodes had MTU 1500 (node-gpu-12). Possible path MTU mismatch when RDMA overlay falls back to TCP.
henry: bingo — I see RDMA logs too: verbs layer complaining about qp timeout and then NIC falling back. /var/log/messages shows:
```
Mar  3 11:35:55 node-gpu-12 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: mlx5_ib: QP 0x2d7 rc timeout, retry_cnt exceeded
Mar  3 11:35:55 node-gpu-12 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: fall back to GNI/TCP path
```
liam: path MTU mismatch + inconsistent jumbo config + RDMA fallback explains variable latency during high small-packet bursts (batching window generates many short inter-GPU messages).
sasha: ops: can we temporarily disable RDMA on the pool while we triage? Maybe force TCP and consistent MTU to flatten behavior.
infra-oncall: ACK — preparing a maintenance plan. Suggestion: 1) cordon node-gpu-12, drain non-critical pods 2) set mtu=9000 on node-gpu-12's host interfaces 3) ensure kernel module params consistent across pool (mlx5_core log_level and retry counts) 4) run iperf + ibv_rc_pingpong to validate RDMA after change.
rita: before touching production, quick mitigation: disable GRO/LRO on the host NICs to see if coalescing interacts badly with jumbo frames. Command:
```
# disable GRO/LRO
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off gso off
```
liam: good call — disabling GRO dropped p95 from ~70ms -> ~8ms in our canary for 2 batches. Sharing numbers soon.
sasha: thanks — go ahead with non-intrusive steps (GRO off) first, then we can schedule MTU fix. Keep notes for postmortem.
ops-bot: ACTION: runbook started: runbook/ew-latency-jumbo-mtu-176451 created by infra-oncall.
henry: after GRO off, kernel tx/rx counters look stable, and tcp_retransmits stopped spiking. Re-running ib tests now.
rita: ibv_rc_pingpong shows stable RDMA once MTU consistent. But we need to ensure CNI overlay isn't rewriting MTU on certain nodes (looking at calico config).
liam: created PR to add an admission check in node-setup to enforce host MTU=9000 for gpu pools (link: https://git.internal/pr/3274).
sasha: timeline: 11:30 anomaly starts; 11:36 identified MTU mismatch + RDMA fallbacks; 11:50 GRO disabled on affected hosts; 12:05 p95 back to baseline.
infra-oncall: Postmortem note: root cause likely inconsistent MTU across node provisioning + RDMA fallback path causing retransmit storms during high small-packet workloads. Next steps: automation to enforce MTU at bootstrap, audit existing pools, and add alert for mlx5 ib fallback events.
liam: I'll follow up with a firmware/driver roll plan for mlx5 on the affected rack — might eliminate flaps.
sasha: awesome — great fast triage everyone. I'll file a short incident summary for management. :thumbsup:
henry: added logs and packet captures to the incident folder: https://internal/incident/176451/pcaps
rita: closing the thread once PRs merge and automation is in place.
ops-bot: RESOLVED: alert east-west-p95 cleared at 1764512760.
